answer.rationale: c2 confirms the low-cost vendor delivered last year (accurate invoicing, quick onboarding, real unit-cost reduction) — directly relevant to trusting their quote now. c4 confirms that renegotiating rather than passively renewing has historically moved incumbents on price AND terms, so the renewal path is not the only lever. The 18% mandate and the contract's non-auto-renewal in 14 days make the low-cost vendor's standalone-meeting quote the cleanest path to TCO reduction; staying with the incumbent would require either a deep concession or restructuring, which c4 shows is possible but not guaranteed in a single cycle. The 94% utilization with no buffer argues against adding a second source (c3 logic) or deferring (c5 logic adds supply risk on top of contract expiry). Renegotiating (c4-style) is a reasonable secondary lever but does not on its own guarantee the 18% cut the mandate requires, and c6's multi-year incumbent commitment is a bigger structural change than one cycle allows.
